docs.title: rgeomex
docs.text:
Geographic boundaries of Mexico (states, municipalities, localities, AGEB, blocks and electoral sections) from INEGI 2019 and INE 2020, and functions to extract the AGEB, blocks and electoral sections of a locality. It is the Python version of the R package rgeomex, part of the dengueverse.

import rgeomex

merida = rgeomex.extract_locality(cve_edo="31", locality="Merida")
blocks = rgeomex.extract_blocks(locality="Merida", cve_edo="31")["block"]
len(blocks)   # 15,374 blocks

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
1. Data on demand: each dataset is downloaded the first time it is used, verified (SHA-256) and kept in a local cache.
  2. Split by state: the large datasets (blocks, AGEB, sections) are one file per state, so working with one state downloads only that state.
  3. Same functions as in R: extract_locality(), extract_blocks(), extract_ageb(), extract_sectores() and find_most_similar_string().
  4. Clean data: EPSG:4326, text in UTF-8 and invalid geometries repaired.
  5. GeoParquet + geopandas: every layer is a GeoDataFrame.

docs.title: rgeomex 0.1.0 (2026-11-19)
docs.text:
First release of the Python version of rgeomex.

  1. Functions load(), datasets(), blocks(), block_centroids(), ageb() and sectors().
  2. Functions with the same names and behaviour as in R: extract_locality(), extract_blocks(), extract_ageb(), extract_sectores() and find_most_similar_string().
  3. Data downloaded on demand with pooch, verified with SHA-256 and cached (cache_dir(), clear_cache(), environment variable RGEOMEX_DATA_DIR).
  4. Tests on Linux, macOS and Windows (Python 3.10 and 3.13).

docs.title: Data v1 (2026-11-19)
docs.text:
Release data-v1: 136 GeoParquet files (659 MB) converted from the R package rgeomex 0.1.0.

  1. Blocks, block centroids, AGEB and sections split by state (32 files each).
  2. Text converted from Latin-1 to UTF-8.
  3. Unclosed rings closed and 10 invalid geometries repaired.
  4. Same number of rows as in R.

docs.title: Data sources
docs.text: Please cite also the original sources of the boundaries: INEGI (Marco Geoestadístico; Censo de Población y Vivienda 2020, ITER) and INE (cartografía electoral 2020).

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
Dataset Content Source Split by state Rows AGEE_inegi19_mx States INEGI 2019 no 32 AGEM_inegi19_mx Municipalities INEGI 2019 no 2,465 AGEM_inegi25_mx Municipalities INEGI 2025 no 2,478 loc_inegi19_mx Urban localities INEGI 2019 no 4,553 iter_2020_loc Localities (ITER) with population, table INEGI, Census 2020 no 189,432 AGEB_inegi_2019 Urban AGEB INEGI 2019 yes 62,732 blocks_ine20_mx Blocks (manzanas) INE 2020 yes 1,556,070 blocks_ine20_mx_centroid Centroids of the blocks INE 2020 yes 1,556,070 sectores_ine20_mx Electoral sections INE 2020 yes 68,436 hrl_mx Layer of rgeomex no 150 pua_mx Layer of rgeomex no 111 ua_mx Layer of rgeomex no 658

The datasets split by state need cve_edo (INEGI key, "01" to "32"):

rgeomex.blocks("31")                 # Yucatán
rgeomex.ageb(["31", "23"])           # Yucatán and Quintana Roo
rgeomex.load("sectores_ine20_mx", cve_edo=20)

docs.title: How the files were made
docs.text:
The files were converted from rgeomex (R) with the scripts in data-raw/:

  1. 01_export_from_r.R exports each dataset and converts the text from Latin-1 to UTF-8.
  2. 02_build_parquet.py splits the large datasets by state, writes GeoParquet (zstd), repairs the invalid geometries (10 in total) and writes the registry of SHA-256 checksums.

The row counts are the same as in R.

docs.title: rgeomex en español
docs.text:
Límites geográficos de México (estados, municipios, localidades, AGEB, manzanas y secciones electorales) del INEGI 2019 y el INE 2020, y funciones para extraer las AGEB, manzanas y secciones electorales de una localidad. Es la versión en Python del paquete de R rgeomex, parte del dengueverse.

Los datos se descargan bajo demanda: la primera vez que se usa un conjunto se descarga del release de GitHub, se verifica (SHA-256) y se guarda en una caché local. Los conjuntos grandes están partidos por estado: si trabajas con un estado, solo se descarga ese estado.

docs.title: Instalación
docs.text: pip install rgeomex

docs.title: Uso
docs.text:
import rgeomex

estados = rgeomex.load("AGEE_inegi19_mx")
municipios = rgeomex.load("AGEM_inegi19_mx", cve_edo="31")

merida = rgeomex.extract_locality(cve_edo="31", locality="Merida")
manzanas = rgeomex.extract_blocks(locality="Merida", cve_edo="31")["block"]

Las funciones tienen los mismos nombres que en R: extract_locality(), extract_blocks(), extract_ageb(), extract_sectores() y find_most_similar_string(). El nombre de la localidad se busca de forma aproximada, así que "Merida" encuentra "Mérida". Para la Ciudad de México (cve_edo="09") se regresan todas sus localidades, igual que en R.

Todas las capas están en EPSG:4326 y el texto en UTF-8. La lista de conjuntos está en Datasets y la documentación de cada función en Reference.

docs.title: 1. A locality and its blocks on a map
docs.text:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import rgeomex

out = rgeomex.extract_blocks(locality="Merida", cve_edo="31")

ax = out["locality"].plot(color="whitesmoke", edgecolor="gray", figsize=(7, 7))
out["block"].boundary.plot(ax=ax, color="steelblue", linewidth=0.1)
ax.set_title(f"Mérida: {len(out['block']):,} blocks (INE 2020)")
ax.set_axis_off()
plt.show()

docs.title: 2. Blocks within 400 m of a point
docs.text:
The flight range of Aedes aegypti (about 400 m) around a point, in metres with the Mexico ITRF2008 / LCC projection (EPSG:6372):

import geopandas as gpd
from shapely.geometry import Point
import rgeomex

blocks = rgeomex.blocks("31").to_crs(6372)
point = gpd.GeoSeries([Point(-89.62, 20.97)], crs=4326).to_crs(6372)
zone = point.buffer(400).union_all()

near = blocks[blocks.intersects(zone)]
len(near)

docs.title: 3. Population of the localities (ITER 2020)
docs.text:
iter_2020_loc is a table with the population of every locality (2020 Census). Its keys build the 9-digit CVEGEO of the locality polygons:

import rgeomex

iter_loc = rgeomex.load("iter_2020_loc")
iter_loc["CVEGEO"] = iter_loc["entidad"] + iter_loc["mun"] + iter_loc["loc"]

loc = rgeomex.load("loc_inegi19_mx", cve_edo="31")
loc = loc.merge(iter_loc[["CVEGEO", "pobtot"]], on="CVEGEO", how="left")
loc[["NOMGEO", "pobtot"]].sort_values("pobtot", ascending=False).head()

docs.title: 4. Several states at once
docs.text:
peninsula = rgeomex.ageb(["04", "23", "31"])   # Campeche, Quintana Roo, Yucatán
peninsula.groupby("CVE_ENT").size()

docs.title: 5. Municipalities: 2019 and 2025
docs.text:
m19 = rgeomex.load("AGEM_inegi19_mx", cve_edo="07")
m25 = rgeomex.load("AGEM_inegi25_mx", cve_edo="07")
set(m25["NOMGEO"]) - set(m19["NOMGEO"])        # new municipalities of Chiapas

docs.title: 6. Export to other formats
docs.text:
out = rgeomex.extract_blocks(locality="Merida", cve_edo="31")
out["block"].to_file("merida_blocks.gpkg")       # GeoPackage (QGIS, R)
out["block"].to_file("merida_blocks.shp")        # shapefile

docs.title: 7. Several localities: a metropolitan area
docs.text:
locality accepts one name or a list of names. With a list, the functions return all the localities, and the AGEB, blocks or sections that intersect any of them:

import rgeomex

amg = ["Guadalajara", "Zapopan", "Tonalá", "Tlaquepaque"]

loc = rgeomex.extract_locality(cve_edo="14", locality=amg)
loc[["CVEGEO", "NOMGEO"]]

out = rgeomex.extract_ageb(locality=amg, cve_edo="14")
len(out["ageb"])

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install rgeomex
# development version
pip install git+https://github.com/fdzul/rgeomex-py

rgeomex needs Python 3.10 or later; it installs geopandas, pyarrow and pooch.

docs.title: Load a dataset
docs.text:
import rgeomex

rgeomex.datasets()                                   # the available datasets

states = rgeomex.load("AGEE_inegi19_mx")             # 32 states
mun = rgeomex.load("AGEM_inegi19_mx", cve_edo="31")  # municipalities of Yucatán

The state key (cve_edo) is the INEGI key, "01" to "32"; 31, "31" or "031" are all accepted.

docs.title: Extract a locality
docs.text:
merida = rgeomex.extract_locality(cve_edo="31", locality="Merida")

The name is found approximately (Levenshtein distance, case insensitive), so "Merida" finds "Mérida". If two names are equally close, None is returned with a warning, as in R. For Mexico City (cve_edo="09") all its localities are returned.

docs.title: Blocks, AGEB and sections of a locality
docs.text:
out = rgeomex.extract_blocks(locality="Merida", cve_edo="31")
out["locality"]   # boundary of the locality
out["block"]      # blocks (INE 2020) that intersect it

rgeomex.extract_ageb(locality="Merida", cve_edo="31")["ageb"]
rgeomex.extract_sectores(locality="Merida", cve_edo="31")["sectores"]

docs.title: The cache
docs.text:
The first time a dataset is used it is downloaded from the GitHub release; later it is read from the cache.

rgeomex.cache_dir()    # e.g. ~/Library/Caches/rgeomex on macOS
rgeomex.clear_cache()  # delete the downloaded files

To use another folder, or a folder that already has the files (offline use), set the environment variable RGEOMEX_DATA_DIR before importing rgeomex:

export RGEOMEX_DATA_DIR=/path/to/rgeomex_data

docs.title: Data
docs.text: The geographic boundaries are created by official government institutions of Mexico, INEGI and INE, and keep their original terms of use. The INEGI information is public under its terms of free use.

docs.title: Maps
docs.text:
Interactive maps of the polygons of rgeomex, from the whole country down to the blocks of the metropolitan area of Guadalajara (the localities of Guadalajara, Zapopan, Tlaquepaque and Tonalá). Each map shows the code that makes it; zoom in and hover over a polygon to see its keys.

The maps were made with .explore() of geopandas; the script that builds them is docs/make_maps.py.

import rgeomex

amg = ["Guadalajara", "Zapopan", "Tonalá", "Tlaquepaque"]

docs.title: States
docs.text:
states = rgeomex.load("AGEE_inegi19_mx")
states.explore(column="NOMGEO", legend=False)

docs.title: Municipalities
docs.text:
The 125 municipalities of Jalisco; the four of the metropolitan area in colour.

mun = rgeomex.load("AGEM_inegi19_mx", cve_edo="14")
mun.explore(tooltip=["CVE_MUN", "NOMGEO"])

docs.title: Localities
docs.text:
loc = rgeomex.extract_locality(cve_edo="14", locality=amg)
loc.explore(column="NOMGEO")

docs.title: AGEB
docs.text:
The urban AGEB (INEGI 2019) that intersect the four localities, coloured by the locality where they fall.

ageb = rgeomex.extract_ageb(locality=amg, cve_edo="14")
ageb["ageb"].explore(tooltip=["CVEGEO"])

docs.title: Blocks
docs.text:
The blocks (INE 2020) of the four localities, about 40,000 polygons; the map can take a few seconds to load.

blocks = rgeomex.extract_blocks(locality=amg, cve_edo="14")
blocks["block"].explore(tooltip=["seccion", "manzana"])

docs.title: Load
docs.text:
Load a dataset by its name in rgeomex (R).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default dataset str

Name of the dataset, e.g. "AGEE_inegi19_mx" or "blocks_ine20_mx" (see :func:datasets).

required cve_edo (str, int or list)

INEGI state key(s). Required for the datasets split by state (AGEB_inegi_2019, blocks_ine20_mx, blocks_ine20_mx_centroid, sectores_ine20_mx); for the whole datasets it filters the rows of the state when the dataset has a CVE_ENT or entidad column.

None

Table of the available datasets.

INE 2020 blocks (manzanas) of one or several states.

Centroids of the INE 2020 blocks of one or several states.

INEGI 2019 AGEB of one or several states.

INE 2020 electoral sections (secciones) of one or several states.

docs.title: Extract
docs.text:
Boundary of one or several localities (INEGI 2019), found by their approximate name.

locality is a name or a list of names, e.g. ["Guadalajara", "Zapopan", "Tonalá", "Tlaquepaque"]. For Mexico City (cve_edo = "09") all its localities are returned.

Blocks (INE 2020) that intersect one or several localities: {"locality", "block"}.

AGEB (INEGI 2019) that intersect one or several localities: {"locality", "ageb"}.

Sections (INE 2020) that intersect one or several localities: {"locality", "sectores"}.

Most similar string of t for each string of s (Levenshtein).

Same behaviour as rgeomex::find_most_similar_string() in R: returns None when no string is within max_dist or when there is a tie (unless feeling_lucky=True, which returns the first one).

docs.text:
